dialogues.speaker: Latkin
dialogues.text: *sigh* Not a single record in any of these documents...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What are you looking for?

dialogues.speaker: Latkin
dialogues.text: Ah... Forgive me, I didn't mean to disturb you. I'm searching for some medical records.

dialogues.speaker: Latkin
dialogues.text: It's for my daughter... She suffers from a rare disease. The moment she leaves the tundra, her consciousness begins to slip away just like melting snowflakes.

dialogues.speaker: Latkin
dialogues.text: And this is even the best that the kind Augury Bird couple could achieve after treating my daughter for over a decade. If they hadn't taken Mirria in right after she was born, she would have...

dialogues.speaker: Latkin
dialogues.text: Even now, she still has to return to the countryside periodically to receive their treatment.

dialogues.speaker: Latkin
dialogues.text: That's why I'm seeking a way to cure her once and for all.

dialogues.speaker: Latkin
dialogues.text: Not just for Mirria, but for our other daughter... to whom we are so deeply indebted.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Best of luck to you.

dialogues.speaker: Latkin
dialogues.text: Thank you.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You have another daughter?

dialogues.speaker: Latkin
dialogues.text: Yes... When that couple took Yeshina with them, they entrusted their daughter to us. Her name is Linnea.

dialogues.speaker: Latkin
dialogues.text: For some reason... that girl could only grow up in human society. Otherwise, she would have suffered unimaginable pain.

dialogues.speaker: Latkin
dialogues.text: I used to be a naturalist, so I happen to know a thing or two about these matters. An "exchange of lives" like this was never meant to be known by humans. Otherwise, the original arrangement would lose its purpose.

dialogues.speaker: Latkin
dialogues.text: It wasn't until a few years ago that we finally realized she was a switched child.

dialogues.speaker: Latkin
dialogues.text: At the time, all we could think about was getting our own daughter back, which is why we were completely blinded to the deeper truth of it all. And on the other hand, Linnea would feel deeply uncomfortable the moment she got anywhere near the tundra...

dialogues.speaker: Latkin
dialogues.text: We knew she would only hold us back if we tried to move faster, so we left her alone back in Nod-Krai.

dialogues.speaker: Latkin
dialogues.text: It was only later that we realized how selfish, how incredibly foolish we had been.

dialogues.speaker: Latkin
dialogues.text: Even if we aren't bound by blood, she is still our daughter, who loved and trusted us unconditionally. She did nothing wrong, yet we...

dialogues.speaker: Latkin
dialogues.text: That is why... I want to cure Mirria as soon as possible. Once she's fully recovered, we're going back to Nod-Krai to find Linnea, and try to make up for a mistake that can never truly be undone.
